theLicenceDecision.rejectedAndWhatItWouldHaveNeeded: Cutting the three situs rails (`situsCity`, `situsZip`, `situsState`) over to the record path. A readable roll city is never replaced. Nothing is invented; nothing is relabelled; no ZIP is ever composed. The named city is stamped `situsCityBasis: "city-limits"` so no renderer can present it as the roll's mailing city.

threeQuestionGate.whatTriggersIt: A payload whose `baseFacts.situsCity` is a DECLARED `absent-verified` absence (an object with that `verdict`, `verdict` read before `status` — the order the probe reads it) while the payload's own served `cityLimitsFact` is `incorporated` and names a city. No new read path and no new write: it re-reads the declaration the payload already carries and the city-limits fact the same payload already serves. In LDT the extra read (`loadCityLimitsFactForServe`) fires ONLY for that shape, so a stub whose payload states its own roll city reads nothing new and its label is byte-identical.
threeQuestionGate.whatFailsWhenAnUnlicensedCityIsNamed: Three instruments, in order of strength. (1) The row itself: `X2-address` FAILs a payload that claims a city-limits city its own `cityLimitsFact` does not license, or claims one over an `unincorporated` answer — proven in the self-test in both directions, with the licensed shape as the control that keeps the new FAIL from firing on the fix's own output. (2) The unit suites: the licence's falsifiers fail in both repos if a bare null, a `lookup-failed`, a `not-applicable`, an unincorporated answer, an unmeasured answer or an incorporated answer with no name ever licenses a city. (3) The customer surface: a city named without its basis would be rendered as the roll's mailing city, which is the misstatement the note and the basis field exist to prevent — and the card row prints the note from the same field, so the two cannot disagree.
threeQuestionGate.whatBypassesIt: Named, not silent: (1) any surface that composes its own address line — the PDF does, and this row does not touch it; (2) the seven absent-situs parcels serve NO composed address at all (X6/XD-7), so there is no line to carry a city; (3) a payload that never serves a `cityLimitsFact` (or serves it unmeasured) names no city — the licence cannot fire, which is the correct no-op, and the line keeps its state+pZIP; (4) the MCP's own gate: without a bearer the MCP half of the row is UNMEASURED, a measurement bypass this close states rather than paper over; (5) the probe's copy of the rule is a THIRD repository's copy that P-331 cannot read — named, not pinned; (6) a payload that states its own readable roll city bypasses the licence entirely, by design.

fleetMemory.LESSON: A licence whose CONDITION is right and whose EVIDENCE PATH is wrong looks exactly like a licence that never fires. Here the condition (`absent-verified` roll city + incorporated city-limits answer) was correct and had been for a day; what was wrong was WHICH SERVED PATH it read the verdict from (the record cell, while the reader serves those rails `legacy-transitional`). Before changing a gate's condition, measure the path its evidence actually arrives on — and prefer the payload's own declaration, which is path-independent, over the path that happened to serve it first.

A cross-repo pin cannot land with the declaration it pins. A row reads the SIBLING'S MAIN, so a row shipped alongside its declaration exits 2 (REFUSE — never a pass, but a REQUIRED check) on both PRs before either merges and on whichever merges first: a red no single merge clears, i.e. a dead gate. Declarations first (green, one commit per repo), rows second (also green). P-331's header now carries this ordering rule; it is worth applying to every future pin.
